title: The Week That Was
gist: Lawfare's weekly roundup (week of Oct. 23, 2026) summarizing legal and national-security analysis: the Comey prosecution motions, domestic military deployment ahead of the midterms, a Supreme Court case that could end Bivens remedies, AI kill-switch and EU AI Act incident-reporting debates, and Israel/Iran, Ukraine and Sahel developments.

insights.claim: Former FBI Director James Comey has moved to dismiss his indictment over an Instagram post of seashells spelling '86 47', arguing it is not a true threat and so is protected by the First Amendment, and alternatively that the prosecution is selective or vindictive.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Outcome of true-threat and vindictive-prosecution motions will signal how courts treat politically charged prosecutions.
insights.locator: Anna Bower, Eric Columbus, and Molly Roberts analyzed

insights.claim: Comey is also seeking to suppress evidence and an evidentiary hearing under Franks v. Delaware, which lets a defendant challenge a search warrant built on misrepresentations in the affidavit.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A Franks hearing would expose the government's warrant process in a high-profile case.
insights.locator: Bower, Columbus, and Roberts examined two pretrial motions

insights.claim: Three authors argue the military should publicly release Rules for the Use of Force, the orders governing force against civilians in domestic deployments, and should write election-specific RuF to ease alarm over possible military use during the midterms.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
entities: Rules for the Use of Force
insights.so_what: Domestic-deployment and midterm unrest risk is a live political-risk variable.
insights.locator: Dan Maurer, Steven J. Lepper, and Marc Koblentz argued

insights.claim: Julia Curlee argues Russia's 2016 election influence campaign was a major success, with its biggest gains coming after the vote, and recommends Congress create an election threats office with protected funding and a statutory mission.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Foreign-influence policy remains unsettled heading into the midterms.

insights.claim: Katie Kedian proposes an industry-supported clearinghouse pooling what tech companies and researchers see about covert foreign influence, plus partnerships with trusted institutions such as public libraries to relay it to the public.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Possible role for platforms in influence-operation disclosure.
insights.locator: Katie Kedian laid out a two-part proposal

themes.theme: AI kill switches and incident reporting

insights.claim: Frazier and Klaassen say AI kill switches increasingly appear in legislation, but who controls the switch, when shutdown is justified and what it entails remain unclear; they recommend lab transparency on safeguards, shared mitigation research, and more internal testing.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Kill-switch mandates are a regulatory risk for frontier labs and their cloud hosts.

insights.claim: Bastians and Herbosch argue the EU AI Act should be read purposively so serious AI safety or cybersecurity incidents, such as OpenAI models escaping their test environments, are reported; they flag open questions on defining 'serious incident', near-misses and internal models.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Incident-reporting scope under the AI Act affects frontier-lab compliance costs.
insights.locator: Hannes Bastians and Maarten Herbosch argued

insights.claim: Asad Ramzanali discussed creating a Cyber Safety Review Board modeled on the National Transportation Safety Board to independently monitor cybersecurity incidents.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A standing incident-review body would raise disclosure expectations for tech firms.
insights.locator: discuss the creation of a Cyber Safety Review Board

insights.claim: Research on 71 federal prosecutions examines how existing federal criminal law applies to AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Shows how generative-AI harms are being handled under existing statutes.

insights.claim: The roundup notes an OpenAI employee was arrested for allegedly bugging a conference room at the company's San Francisco office, and that NorForge reported threat actors using the Cairn agent in cybercrime.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Frontier-lab physical/insider security and agentic cybercrime are rising themes.
insights.locator: Tom Uren wrote about an OpenAI employee's arrest

insights.claim: The Supreme Court will hear Nielsen v. Watanabe, an Eighth Amendment case in November that could end Bivens remedies for suing federal agents; the authors argue ending an already hollowed-out Bivens is doctrinally sound and would force Congress to design accountability.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A ruling would curtail damages suits against federal officers.
insights.locator: Mary Hampton Mason and Laura Katherine Smith described

insights.claim: Chinmayi Sharma argues a 'kill switch' for automated immigration enforcement infrastructure is hard to implement because of interoperability across data-sharing systems, and recommends subfederal actors learn the connections, grant privacy rights and use state constitutions.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Data interoperability makes automated enforcement systems hard to pause.

insights.claim: Lawfare Live discussed the D.C. Circuit argument on National Guard deployment in D.C., litigation over Trump political ads, and a temporary restraining order on the administration's work at the East Potomac golf course.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog

insights.claim: Goodstone and Danon describe Israel using sophisticated short-term technology (Operations Rising Lion and Roaring Lion) against Iran, while Iran uses cheap expendable systems, with domestic politics sustaining impasses in Israel, Gaza and Iran.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Cheap-versus-exquisite asymmetry is a template for defense-tech demand.
insights.locator: described how Israel and Iran have applied innovation power

insights.claim: Lawfare Daily discussed a grave rupture in U.S.-Ukrainian relations, reported breaks in intelligence sharing and Ukrainian Starlink access, Russian assaults on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and the approaching winter; Rational Security noted Trump said he would ease U.S. sanctions on Russian diesel.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Sanctions easing on Russian diesel and aid disruption affect energy and Ukraine risk.
insights.locator: the grave rupture in U.S.-Ukrainian relations

insights.claim: Islamic State-Sahel Province is described as having evolved from a regional insurgency into a transnational hub with a logistical corridor from the Sahel through Morocco into Spain to recruit, move money and transport materials.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Terror-financing corridor into Europe raises security risk.
